authoritative_for: Chancery owns structural validation of installed provider bundles, complete installed catalog presentation, exact-ID promise resolution, and documentation-contract compatibility reporting.
Each Chancery invocation canonicalizes each encountered provider selector once to build one in-memory registry view and identifies the exact provider, entry, and manual bytes used as its basis.
not_authoritative_for: Owning products remain authoritative for capability semantics, effects, current runtime behavior, live readiness, authorization, and domain success.
The interactive agent, not Chancery, interprets a user's natural-language request and selects plausible entries.

covers: All supported public Chancery CLI outcomes for installed catalog discovery, exact contract reading, exact-ID promise resolution, registry validation, and provider publication in this release.
excludes: Help and version display, implementation helpers, provider-product behavior, live readiness probes, semantic request matching, and represented capability invocation are outside this inventory claim.

shared_access_and_trust: Chancery reads only the selected local registry and explicitly indexed regular files beneath fixed provider bundle roots.
Catalog presence and resolution do not grant access to or authorize any represented interface.
shared_privacy_and_retention: Provider documentation is processed locally in memory and Chancery retains no registry, query, dossier, or runtime state.
Provider bundles must not contain credentials, secrets, private source material, or transient runtime output.
compatibility_and_retirement: Provider schema version identifies bundle shape, provider release identifies the owning release, and entry contract version identifies documented semantic compatibility.
Schema changes deploy reader-first; dependency ranges describe documentation-contract compatibility only.
operational_limits: Resolution is bounded by the installed registry, explicitly indexed files, configured file-size and provider-count limits, and one deterministic transitive dependency walk.
Chancery has no daemon, database, network access, model integration, runtime readiness probe, or execution path for represented interfaces.
